level: CLI native-peer Windows supervisor hardening: bounded stdin relay, handle-ownership transfer and restricted inheritance on the E61 atomic Job admission
componentAcceptance: verified on both real Windows machines with real never-reading and fast-exiting children; the E61 atomic Job, watchdog, framing and identity machinery are unchanged and still green
productAcceptance: partial; process containment by a Job object is not an account/AppContainer/filesystem boundary, and a malicious same-user process remains outside this threat model
implementation: The stdin relay is a bounded BlockingCollection drained by its own thread: a child that stops reading surfaces as a bounded TryAdd timeout, the supervisor answers stopped with reason input-stalled, terminates the Job tree with 137 and still reports treeStopped; a broken pipe only ends the drain and the loop keeps the graceful frame. A synchronous WriteLineAsync().Wait() design was rejected because a synchronously opened handle runs the write inline and the timeout would never fire.
OwnStream transfers raw-handle ownership before FileStream construction, closing the handle exactly once when construction fails, on both pipe ends.

CreateProcess now carries PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST (0x00020002) beside the Job list, so the child inherits exactly its pipe ends plus a private inheritable duplicate of stderr. The constant was reproduced, not assumed: 0x00020001 is a reserved number and both real Windows machines reject it with ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Fixture symmetry: the helper-death matrix gains preCreate (dying before creation must leave no child and no created gate), the legacy gate reclaims a suspended child by exact PID/FILETIME recovered from the raw file when its JSON cannot be parsed, and two new production cases cover a real never-reading child (160x60KB lines into a non-reading hold worker) and relay writes racing a fast child exit.

platforms.cliSuites: 16/16 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (13 job incl. 3 new, 3 probe)

platforms.scope: existing verified fixture; the supervisor, the suite and its fixture dependencies were uploaded via SFTP (the first run failed at load because the fixture lacked the CLI fixture files — fixed by uploading them, then rerun)
suite uploaded to the existing fixture; the Windows-only machinery is an explicit skip there

preservedFailures: The first local run failed all cases with HANDLE_LIST_UPDATE_FAILED because the handle-list attribute constant was wrong (0x00020001 reserved; correct is 0x00020002). The failure was reproduced in minimal standalone scripts on both Windows machines and fixed; nothing was skipped or silenced.
The first Win10 run failed at module load because the fixture lacked the CLI fixture files; they were uploaded and the run rerun to green.
limitations: This is still Job-object process containment: no OS-account, AppContainer, filesystem or seccomp-equivalent boundary is claimed, and the handle list restricts inheritance by a same-user child rather than defending against a malicious same-user process.
The relay queue bound (128 lines, 5s TryAdd) is a supervisory bound, not flow control; a slow-but-reading child that stays under it is unaffected.
CLI real-inference runs, full remote CLI locations, cross-version installers and the complete command/CLI write facade remain open and unchanged.
